Priya: Ran the overnight eviction/shard-simulation across dev cluster (gpus-x4). Dump + small writeup here: https://go/redwood/gists/evict-sim-1800
Priya: TL;DR: 1) 4-shard layout has ~8% better hit-rate for same mem but spikes OOMs under bursty long-prefix traffic. 2) 16-shard reduces peak memory and fragmentation but hurts steady-state hit-rate for hot prefixes. 3) TTL=30s vs TTL=300s: 30s reduces mem by ~22% but increases tail latency due to more cold fetches.
Marcel: Nice. Can you paste the key profiler snippets? want to check workspace peaks vs slab allocations.
Priya: Sure, pasted profiler output below. Note allocations are from two sources: prefix slab and workspace temporaries.
Priya: ```
[GPU0] peak_mem: 24.3GB
  prefix_slab_resident: 10.1GB (52k entries)
  workspace_reserved_pool: 8.5GB (20 concurrent slots)
  fragmentation_loss: 1.8GB
  other (kernels/buffers): 3.9GB
alloc/ops: frequent small allocs during attention kernels when KV cache hit misses occur (especially on long sequences)
```
Aisha: That fragmentation number looks high. Did the allocator get the small-buffer reuse patch? I thought Evan's pool-Coalesce change was merged last week.
Evan: I merged a conservative reuse path (recycle_bin_size=32MB) but we left it off for the prefix slab to avoid cross-contamination. The simulation toggled recycle for workspace only.
Marcel: If workspace reuse is on, why are we still seeing many small allocs? Batching heuristic might be creating variable workspace needs per request. Maybe kernel selection (fused vs unfused matmul) changes temporaries.
Priya: Exactly — we profiled kernel choices during the sim. When runtime picks the fused-attn kernel with reduced workspace, mem drops ~800MB but per-token latency increases ~2.5ms in some shapes. When it picks the baseline kernel, workspace jump is ~1.2GB and latency slightly better. The runtime's kernel selector uses the last-seen seq-len histogram; under bursty long-prefixes it flips to baseline and causes OOM cliff.
Aisha: Hmm. So eviction policy + kernel selector interplay causes the cliff. If we tune eviction to be more aggressive on low-frequency prefixes during kernel-selection wobble, we might avoid that cliff. But that will cost hit-rate.
Evan: Proposal: add a tiny bloom filter per shard to track recently-accessed prefixes (40MB per shard). Use it to protect hot entries during short TTL windows and evict low-frequency cold ones first. Bloom reduces bookkeeping overhead vs full LRU recency list.
Marcel: Simulation results for Bloom idea?
Priya: I ran a micro-experiment: 8-shard + bloom(2 hash, 8e6 bits) + TTL=60s. Results: peak_mem +10% vs plain 8-shard, hit-rate +6%, OOMs eliminated in 97% of burst windows. Tradeoff: bloom false positives keep some cold prefixes alive (worse mem).
Evan: Sounds promising. Another lever: shrink workspace reserved pool when median seq-len < threshold. e.g., workspace_reserve_pct: 20 -> 10 when median_seq < 256. That frees 1.6GB on average.
Priya: Config we used in sim:```
prefix_cache: { shards: 8, shard_size_mb: 12000, ttl_seconds: 60, bloom_bits: 8e6, bloom_hashes: 2 }
workspace: { reserve_pool_slots: 20, reserve_pct: 20, reuse_recycle_bin_mb: 32 }
allocator: { max_bin: 128MB, coalesce: true }
```
Aisha: Could we make the kernel selector aware of current free_workspace_mem? So it biases toward lower-workspace kernel if projected workspace + slab > threshold. That avoids unexpected flips.
Evan: Yeah we can add a soft budget check: before kernel pick, estimate workspace_needed(seq_len, batch) and if (available_workspace < margin) prefer low-workspace kernel. Margin tunable per-SLO.
Marcel: We should also consider shard sizing tunables per-model. For models with long-context traffic (code assistants), use fewer shards with larger slab but higher protection for hot prefixes. For chat-heavy models with many short prefixes, more shards to reduce fragmentation.
Priya: Action items from sim:
- Aisha/Evan: prototype kernel-selector budget check (small change) — target branch: runtime/kernel-budget-guard. ETA: 2d.
- Evan: run bloom-filter per-shard sim at scale (16 nodes) and measure false-positive mem tail. ETA: 3d.
- Priya: run another end-to-end sim with workspace dynamic reserve policy (auto-shrink when median_seq<256 and expand when >512). ETA: 4d.
kv-cache-bot: Simulation summary uploaded to artifact store: s3://redwood-dev/evict-sim/1800012345/ (files: trace.parquet, profile_agg.json, config.yaml) :robot_face:
Marcel: One more ask — include the kernel selection trace in trace.parquet. Need to correlate kernel choice with each eviction window.
Priya: Will add kernel_choice column to next run.
Aisha: If we get the prototype kernel guard, it might remove most cliff OOMs without hurting hit-rate significantly. Let's be conservative with bloom size initially.
Evan: I'll open PRs for both kernel guard and workspace auto-resize. We'll add rollback flags for prod.
Priya: Great. Thanks all. Closing this thread after next sim. :+1:
